title: Lesson 16 - MDM architecture scenarios: traceability, common context for business rules, tooling vs declarative
description: Given a customer scenario, recommend appropriate approaches and techniques to capture and maintain customer reference and metadata to preserve traceability and establish a common context for business rules, and decide when dedicated MDM tooling is warranted versus declarative Salesforce capabilities.

questions.question: A single Salesforce org needs to keep customer records clean from web and phone channels. Which approach is most appropriate FIRST?
options: Adopt an enterprise MDM tool immediately
Use declarative Matching Rules, Duplicate Rules, and external IDs
Build a data warehouse golden record and sync it back
questions.explanation: For a single-org need, declarative on-platform capabilities are the right first step; enterprise tooling (A) and warehouse round-trips (C) are overkill, and manual review (D) does not scale.

questions.question: Which TWO requirements most justify dedicated MDM tooling over declarative Salesforce?
options: Multi-domain, multi-system master data with complex fuzzy matching
A single org with two channels and standard Account matching
Real-time bidirectional sync across many systems with lineage requirements
Keeping a duplicate report scheduled weekly
questions.explanation: Enterprise-scale matching (A) and multi-system real-time sync with lineage (C) justify tooling; single-org/standard matching (B) and duplicate reports (D) do not.

questions.question: What two artifacts are essential to make MDM traceable?
options: A cross-reference (source system + source id) and provenance (winning source/rule)
A page layout and a validation rule
A Big Object and an External Object
A duplicate rule and a report
questions.explanation: Traceability needs the cross-reference to sources and provenance of the winner; the other options are platform features unrelated to tracing master data origin.
